title: Dynamic credit clock and contextual upgrade flow
creator: Asha Verma
description: Run a staged experiment that replaces a fixed trial credit expiry with a dynamic 'credit clock' that decays more slowly for high-quality usage and surfaces contextual upgrade CTAs based on credit velocity. Goal: improve trial-to-paid conversion while preserving unit economics and reducing support tickets about expired credits. This ticket captures the hypothesis, measurement plan, experiment buckets, engineering work, and risk mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment ready behind feature flag and telemetry enabled
Three experiment cohorts instrumented and routed (Control, Slow-decay, Usage-weighted extension)
Dashboard showing activation, 7d/30d conversion, average credit consumption rate, and refunds/support signals
Significant uplift in 14-day conversion or neutral revenue per user with <=5% increase in support volume
Post-experiment rollout playbook and migration strategy for existing credits
experiment_design: Hypothesis: Users who receive small, usage-aligned extensions to trial credits will demonstrate higher intent signals (multi-session, higher prompt depth) and convert at a higher rate than fixed-expiry trials without materially increasing refunded usage.

Cohorts: Control (current fixed 14-day expiry), Cohort A (time-decay slowed by 50% for users with >=3 distinct projects), Cohort B (usage-weighted extension: +20% credit window if average session tokens/day > threshold)
Randomization shard at signup event; deterministic device+user hash to prevent reassignment
Feature flag gating, server-side calculation of decay and extension, client and email triggers for contextual CTA
Sample size target: 12k trial signups per cohort to detect a 15% relative lift in conversion at 80% power
metrics: Primary: Revenue per new trial user (net of credits) over 30 days
Secondary: Average credit consumption rate (tokens/day), sessions per user, feature activation rate (API key usage), upgrade CTA click-through rate
Operational: Support tickets mentioning 'credit expired' and refund rate, billing disputes, SLA for credit extension calculation (<200ms)
rollout_plan: Day 0: Launch behind FF to 5% traffic; smoke tests for correctness and latency
Day 1-3: Increase to 20% if no regression in latency or errors; monitor dashboard and support channel
Day 4-14: Full sampling to reach statistical power targets; daily automated checks for fiscal exposure
Post-win: Canary to 10% of new signups for 7 days with business rules, then full rollout. If mixed results, promote cohort-specific rules into targeting engine
Fallback: Immediate rollback of extensions if billing anomalies or >2x expected refund rate
dependencies: ENG-8271 (billing hooks to record credit grants and expirations)
ADS-210 (experiment dashboard and alerting on conversion metrics)
Legal/Finance signoff for credit policy changes
risks: Higher short-term revenue leakage from aggressive extensions
Increased support volume from perceived unfairness in cohort assignment
Edge cases where expired credits are not reconciled across Dedicated/Private deployments
Complexity in billing reconciliation for customers converting mid-extension
